reviews.text: Pablo Larraín's film portrays a frenzied, haunted woman disintegrating before our eyes - it is a mesmerising triumph.
reviews.author: Francesca Steele

reviews.text: If this is a ‘fable from a true tragedy’, the way Larrain harnesses that tragedy ends up being just another way to define Diana as a victim.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: The protagonist is Diana Spencer like her life, this story does not represent a traditional biopic. The proposal of this “fable of a real tragedy” is to unmask that idyllically called “fairy tale” whose paradigm changed from Diana's experience...
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: Stewart’s performance is a staggering one that does so much more than merely replicate the looks and mannerisms of her historical icon.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: Spencer is a spectacular, rare kind of biopic that portrays its main subject as more fully-fledged than ever before.
reviews.author: Yasmine Kandil

reviews.text: It is like Ridley Scott’s most recent films in which we get to congratulate ourselves for having a single advantage over those who have it better than us in numerous ways, but more textured for the way that it explores mental health
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: Containing one of my favorite scenes of the entire year with the ‘soldier game’ and a masterclass in numerous aspects of filmmaking, including score and cinematography, this is one I will continue to go back to time and time again.
reviews.author: Amy Smith

reviews.text: Pablo Larraín takes an outsider's view of an iconic public figure and gracefully shatters any illusion of what the public thinks of them.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart disappears into her role as Diana, Princess of Wales, during a tense Christmas weekend in the early 1990s. Don't expect fireworks or theatrics — or much in the way of closure — but instead a subtle and effective character study.
reviews.author: Jackson Weaver

reviews.text: Heartened by a career-defining turn by Kristen Stewart, Spencer shows the ephemerality of grandeur, the rigidity of aristocracy, and the enduring humanity of Diana.
reviews.author: Ryan Oquiza

reviews.text: a thoroughly impressive, unforgettable character study that will surprise you and break your heart with the universality of its themes, and that you’ll find yourself revisiting time and time again.
reviews.author: Serena Seghedoni

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart’s CAREER DEFINING PERFORMANCE! Haunting, claustrophobic, intimate, personal, tragic, & all around one of the most unique experiences I’ve seen all year
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: This recent addition to the Dianassance is a refresh and should be used as a map for future biopics.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: Princess Di, it’s overstated, was like a beautiful bird trapped in a gilded cage – a pheasant, to be exact. Pheasants are shown adorning the tapestry above her bed, hunted for sport, and escaping shotgun blasts only to end up roadkill (!!!).
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: Larrain exceeds expectations, as he experiments with surreal narrative elements and ultimately gives us a striking Diana story that we’ve never seen before.
reviews.author: Emma-Jane Betts

reviews.text: Spencer is a horror movie with a twist. This film has the audience root for all of the aspects of horror movies they’re usually yelling at the characters to ignore.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Spencer is about generalizing queerness and about showing how LGBT people are not the only ones in closets. But it’s also careful not to push actual LGBT people back into that windowless room while appropriating their experiences.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: Spencer reaches levels of haunting piquancy and has a performance from Kristen Stewart the encompasses mind, body, and soul.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: This unusual film might not be to everyone’s taste, but it was anything but dull.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: This is the most mature of Stewart's performances to date.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: Without achieving perfection and with a haughty performance from Stewart, Larraín (Jackie) revolves around a woman in a story that opts to be an imaginary version, both dark and luminous... of what could've had happened. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José C. Donayre Guerrero

reviews.text: The film’s intriguing tone, which involves metaphors so heavy-handed that [the writer] couldn’t possibly expect us to take them seriously, feels less like a biopic and more like a campy psychological horror movie. ... And Stewart plays it perfectly.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: Stemming from a weak and disinteresting narrative, the voiceless director plays in the "think whatever you want" safe zone and banks too much in the ambiguity of his stories. Luckily, Kristen Stewart makes [it] bearable... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: An equally bold and sensitive — and enthralling — portrait of England's rose wilting not from the sunlight she craves, but from the royal inferno.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: An exquisite and haunting portrait of a fairy tale gone wrong.
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Without being exceptional, [Spencer] maintains a credible fateful tone that stirs uneasiness, and it's difficult to lose interest in that lost person and her unnerving desolation. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: A fable narrated from a true story perspective. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: The dreamlinke sequences, childhood flashbacks or hallucinations, is what makes this film transcend. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alfonso Flores-Durón y Martínez

reviews.text: Thrilling to watch, both within the dramatic context of the film and in the meta-cinematic context of watching an actress ascend to a higher plane of performance.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text: Stewart's personification is more authentic than what a legion of imitators of Lady Di could have provided, according to the same principle by which a painting by Emil Nolde, more than faithfully reproducing a sunset, speaks about the truth of the light.
reviews.author: Agustín Acevedo Kanopa

reviews.text: SPENCER is a beautiful, tragic and almost horror-like portrait of Princess Diana, which in its focused fiction creates something true and which becomes truly mesmerizing through Kristen Stewarts fantastic performance in the lead.
reviews.author: Jimmy Cage

reviews.text: Although the story is bizarre and unconvincing, theres a fascination in never quite knowing where its going next.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: Larraín again offers an impression of a famous public figure at a time of significant trauma, and is ingeniously able to project over the admittedly fascinating political tale an even more moving existential one.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: Viewer reaction to Spencer will vary in the extremeanyone looking for the empathy or activism that made Diana so beloved and important wont find them here.
reviews.author: David Reddish

reviews.text: To make matters even stranger, Larraín and Knight add an element of magic realism that's even more are odds with their dissonant melding of creative forces...
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Despite the dark moments the film ventures through, the ending is uplifting, similar to the likes of a long exhale. This unconventional Christmas movie will soon become a go-to for many fans of the royal familys history.
reviews.author: Josie Meléndez

reviews.text: Spencer is a moving depiction of one of the worlds most beloved figures brought to life by the ever-talented Pablo Larran and career-best work from Kristen Stewart.
reviews.author: Mark Goodyear

reviews.text: An artistic meditation on the mental prison Diana found herself in, as well as a reminder that she briefly managed to break free.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: SPENCER beguiles and frustrates in equal measure, but Kristen Stewarts performance is definitely the highlight. Like Diana, she's got a mesmerizing quality and charisma that makes the film watchable even during the most tedious moments.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: This is an emotionally devastating capturing of pain and suffering that works both as a focused biopic and larger message.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Spencer ultimately is not just a tragedy of a trapped princess but a downright satirical examination of the monarchy; one that is dependent on propping up an illusion of perfection to the masses.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Like Scrooge in the Dickens story, Stewart's Diana spends the film ruminating on her past, hindered by her present, and dreading the future.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Spencer is worth seeing based on Stewart's impeccable performance and the movie's gorgeous sense of style. However, the movie is a bit lacking regarding its nuance and depth.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart [plays] Diana as a woman of contradictory impulses -- she is fragile one moment, defiant the next. It is a mix of tones the actress pulls off with confidence even as she nails the late princess' mannerisms and speech patterns.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Spencer is a fever dream of a film, yielding a somber vision of the turmoil that Diana went through as a mother and a woman trapped under the strain of her obligations to the Royal Family. It will sit with you for days after seeing it.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: Spencer is a beautiful yet haunting portrayal of the late Princess Diana. Stewart does an incredible job embodying Diana. Not only does she nail the accent and physical presence, but  also eloquently captures a woman who suffered from bulimia.
reviews.author: Marriska Fernandes

reviews.text: It's abysmal to see the gifted likes of Timothy Spall and Sally Hawkins taking one for the team; so don't. Eat your pearls.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart is a nerve-racked Diana, Princess of Wales, who endures a torturous Christmas weekend with her scornful royal in-laws while in a state of glam delirium. Something wicked this way comes? No, it's just the queen, trailed by her corgis.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: Spencer gets up close and personal with its subject, both in director Pablo Larrain's shooting style and in scripter Steven Knight's attempts to analyze and understand the mindset of Diana, Princess of Wales.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Stunning to look at and, with Jonny Greenwood's score, dreamy, evocative and haunting. At times it feels like a horror movie, a Polanski-like mental descent. Don't come for any kind of history lesson; come for the vibe.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Covering a curious mix of genres, Spencer adds up to something weird, fun and interesting.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Spencer is led by strong direction by Pablo Larrain and an amazing performance from Kristen Stewart. It is an effective psychological drama that effectively immerses the audience with its grand bouts of dramatic excess. Highly recommended.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Larrain is an astonishing filmmaker - and he lays out Steven Knight's (Eastern Promises, Dirty Pretty Things) mischievous script in economically assembled scenes.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Starring as Princess Diana in this uniquely unsettling film, Kristen Stewart delivers a performance that places her front and centre of the Oscar race.
reviews.author: Dominic Corry

reviews.text: If nothing else, it's an extremely moving portrait of motherhood and survival in a ghastly, antiquated world -- one that questions those who would pledge themselves to crown or country.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: In a breathless, headlong way, Stewart does a credible job, but she’s perched on the edge of hysteria throughout and the upbeat ending fails to alter the impression that she and Larraín have delivered a one-dimensional portrait of a victim.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Stewart captures the essence of being in an oppressive environment.
reviews.author: Lisa Nesselson

reviews.text: Even in [Pablo] Larraín's unconventional choice to interpret Diana's life rather than re-enact it, [Kristen] Stewart's performance never wavers from evoking the truth.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart is not only a dead ringer for Di, she has captured all of her ticks, speech patterns and mannerisms, right down to the signature head tilt. It's a pretty remarkable performance. As for the film itself, well, it's a bit of a slog.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: In this world of high-toned entertainment, you can flee from the Windsors like Diana Spencer did, and you should.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: A performance that is as natural as it is powerfully melancholic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Brenda Medel

reviews.text: Spencer looks pristine and is shot like a thriller, finding horror in the hallowed halls of royalty but what does it tell us about anything in those halls? Very little.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: We are unconvinced by Kristen Stewart's imitation.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Pablo Larraín's masterful Spencer is one of the most assured, idiosyncratic and wholly satisfying biopics in memory.
reviews.author: Samuel R. Murrian

reviews.text: A visually gorgeous and haunting portrayal of Diana that's filled with metaphors. Fundamentally it's a story about love (and the lack thereof).
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Filmmaker Pablo Larraín creates an atmosphere of dignity and discontent.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart delivers a career-best performance in this dark and haunting fairy tale turned nightmare. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Simultaneously wary and celebratory of biographical limitation, Larraín tweaks the conventions of the genre, ironising idealist conceptions of history through scenes that explore how intensity of feeling can appear like depth of action.
reviews.author: Georgie Carr

reviews.text: It's a film I didn't expect to be impressed by; instead, It has haunted me with its portrayal of a woman increasingly isolated by her emotional and mental distress.
reviews.author: Sarah McMullan

reviews.text: Spencer director Pablo Larraín lasers in on Diana's (Kristen Stewart) horrid time at the Sandringham estate during the 1991 Christmas, delivering a haunting portrait that's more psychological horror than drama at times.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: Stewart was an unlikely but, it's now clear, ingenious choice for the role; she's going through such a period of pronounced anguish that the wrong kind of actor would have played the whole thing as overwrought, and ruined it.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: By exhuming Dynasty Di from her saintly casket, Larraín and Stewart have done the world a great favor.
reviews.author: Grace Lavery

reviews.text: Pablo Larraín's impressionistic portrait of Princess Diana takes big swings that rarely hit.
reviews.author: Orla Smith

reviews.text: As in Diana's life, no doubt, the film's grace notes come when she's talking one-on-one with William and Harry or with a servant.
reviews.author: Chuck Wilson

reviews.text: It's easy to cheer the assertion of autonomy that is the film's chief moral. But it's too easy. And for that reason the movie is cheap, cashing in on maudlin, binary, and oftentimes outright ridiculous sentiments.
reviews.author: David G. Hughes

reviews.text: It's a career-defining moment for Stewart. More than merely mimicking a voice or a walk, you can see it in her face and every mannerism.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Spencer is a portrait of a lady in distress, a biopic less interested in historicity than it is hysteria.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: A devastating portrait of the way things have always been done clashing with the urgency of reality, of a person against a system.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: To call "Spencer" a biopic would be to misunderstand the term because the movie is more of an interpretation of Diana, not her life story.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: Poetic, mysterious and subversively cathartic (...) unequivocally makes clear to all watching why Diana mattered so much, to so many. It has something to do with love.
reviews.author: Milana Vujkov

reviews.text: You don't need simple answers when you're presented with this kind of mood piece, one more intrigued with feeling than a Wikipedia-esque list of facts.
reviews.author: Kayleigh Donaldson

reviews.text: A hit job on Princess Diana, full of scenes that have to be imaginary.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart shines in Pablo Larraín's latest drama Spencer.... It's a tough watch especially for those of us who hold the memory of Princess Diana close to our hearts.
reviews.author: Raquel Stecher

reviews.text: Although Stewart nails her character's tremulousness, the actor is as restricted by Larrain's melodramatic vision as the character is by monarchy. Stewart delivers her lines in a hoarse voice, as though she is in the middle of a prolonged strangulation.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart, an actor I genuinely admire, struggles mightily with the role, and ends up somewhere in between an interesting impersonation and a 5th-grader's notion of a madwoman.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Unlike other overly polished portraits of the Princess of Wales, Spencer aims to humanize Diana in ways that aren't always entirely flattering.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: Visually captivating, with Kristen Stewart at the apogee of her career. [Full
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The filmmaking is superb and Stewart delivers a heartbreaking performance to complement the visuals' fractured psyche of hallucinatory suffering.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: It's unsettling, claustrophobic, intimate, endowed with a certain lavishness in the sets and wardrobe, but, above all, illuminated at all times by a brilliant performance from Kristen Stewart. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: A disturbing exercise in style about loneliness and social cannibalism. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Fernandez

reviews.text: Stewart offers here an Oscar-worthy performance, while Larraín once again confirms his talent for tackling this type of story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Kristin Stewart, Timothy Spall and Sallie Hawkins all turn in fine performances in this well-acted film. The sets and costumes also have the quality one expects. Jacqueline Durran's costume designs are among this awards season favorites.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Spencerdoesn't captivate, it haunts.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: There are films that you would normally consider character studies in general, and then there are films like Spencer in which the character and the performance are the film.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Rather than celebrate her and her life, Larraín can only seem to memorialize her as a fragile victim, filling his film with constant references to death, as if anyone could forget the horrific circumstances of Diana's end.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Everything in the film is done well, and for explicable reasons. But justifications do not a masterpiece make.
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: n imagined weekend during which Princess Diana tries to escape the prison of life as a royal.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Powered by a singular, searing performance by Kristen Stewart, Spencer aims not for imitation or adherence to history, but persuasive evocation.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: An interesting exercise in claustrophobia, tension and even horror, starring an amazing Kristen Stewart. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: At times frustratingly abstract, Spencer is not grand in scope, but in its concept and storytelling. It also features one of the very best lead performances of the year.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Spencer is every woman's story, who's grown tired of living a lie. It breaks our notions of privilege and happiness. Diana had it all... beauty, wealth, and family, but it all came at the cost of her own freedom and identity.
reviews.author: Renuka Vyavahare

reviews.text: Spencer rips into the British monarchy with great élan, using sympathy for the so-called "people's princess" to throw us into an enjoyable tizzy of horror at the royals...
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: This is anxiety filmmaking at its finest.
reviews.author: George Clark

reviews.text: Leave it to actor Stewart to save the day. Ninety percent of the time she brings the spirit and look of Princess Di back to earth in an eerily real performance that captures the spirit of Buckingham Palace's most rebellious daughter-in-law.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: The enterprise is saved by Stewart, who has mastered Diana's winsome side glance and that throaty, almost strangled voice that always tipped us off as to how miserable she was.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: "Spencer" becomes a fascinating showcase for Stewart, giving the toughest and most brilliant performance of her career. She captures the fragility and, eventually, the maternal ferocity that made Diana a people's princess.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: A Big Mac of tabloid analysis served on a sterling silver tray. It isn't that the emperor wears no clothes, but that the clothes are the circus wardrobe of the Daily Mail and The Express. "Spencer" is a movie that feeds on the corpse it seeks to sanctify.
reviews.author: Ray Greene

reviews.text: The actress, in her best performance so far, makes us feel the anguish of the character at the banquets, her marital frustration, the absolute claustrophobia on that estate. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Janire Zurbano

reviews.text: 'Spencer' is not a fairy story; in fact, many of its scenes and sequences feel more like horror. As a meditation on the crisis of mental health that Princess Diana lived through, it's devastatingly effective. And Stewart is stunning.
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: ...aggressively uneventful...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: A story of a well-etched individual person who feels crushed into oblivion by the sheer force of history all around her.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Very much a ghost story, but not a typical one; it is a tender and prickly like a raw wound, abstract and unsettling, yet full of emotional grace notes that cut deep.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: With Spencer, Pablo Larraín revalidates his status as an iconoclast director. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gustavo Herrera Taboada

reviews.text: Meant to subvert more standard royal depictions but without much more to offer, this effort at empathy and humanization proves both obvious and dully repetitious, undeserving the considerable talent on hand.
reviews.author: George Elkind

reviews.text: A fresh look to Diana of Gales. Hope in a hopeless place. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillem Martinez Oya

reviews.text: A condensed biopic that also functions as a psychological horror film...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Larraín isn't concerned with showcasing the events we all know, instead creating a layered portrait and finding the truths in both her public and private persona.
reviews.author: Amelia Harvey

reviews.text: If anything, the film demonstrates the determination Diana had for her own stable mental health and happiness, despite the pressures of her royal life
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: The most haunting film of the year. Spencer is how you make a terrifying and unnerving film but remain arthouse and posh.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: An extremely competent movie with plenty of positives. At times it's touching and at others, it's very on the nose but it never felt truly balanced or enticing.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: This artful, well-acted alienation is both clean-cut and oblique, as well as frivolous and amusing in spots.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Dull and empty of any emotional connection this is over the top art, it's got nothing to say of any real value but it says it way too loudly. Most of all, it's rather highly disrespectful to the memory of such a beloved figure.
reviews.author: Zehra Phelan

reviews.text: Larraín has again upended the biopic genre, much like Diana did the British royal family.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: What must it be like for an actor to play a famous person, let alone one this impossibly famous? The challenge starts with resemblance, and Stewart gets Diana's wounded-deer manner, the sulky eyes, the slight tilt of the head.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Spencer is one of the best, if not the best, films of the year, grounded by a career standout performance from Kristen Stewart.
reviews.author: Stephanie Archer

reviews.text: Larraín presents a vision that is singular and arresting, placing much of his film's success on the shoulders of his leading lady, who absolutely delivers.
reviews.author: Natasha Alvar

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart fills big shoes as Lady Di in this tightly focused immersion into the inner turmoil of (another) woman under duress and at the breaking point.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: With his latest, Larraín continues to make fascinating strides in historically-based fiction filmmaking, stretching the genre in ways we can only hope other filmmakers pick up and experiment with.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Spencer may not have anything new or revelatory to say about Diana herself, but its visual language says a lot about how she's become part of our modern myths.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Actor Stewart contributes an odd, but defensible, impersonation here. Hawkins' Maggie, Timothy Spall's officious lackey Major Gregory and Sean Harris' royal chef de cuisine, however, deserve lavish praise.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: Overall, Spencer is a beautifully crafted and introspective look at Diana, and at the very least certainly serves its purpose as a claustrophobic character study.
reviews.author: Gemma Creagh

reviews.text: If Spencer is supposed to be a sort of tribute to the memory of a tragic woman victimised by an archaic industry I'd truly hate to see what a condemnation would have looked like.
reviews.author: Hanna Flint

reviews.text: In Spencer, we see Stewart in a version of one of Diana's diaphanous white gowns - except she's wearing it while bent over a toilet to vomit. Playing one of the most famous and glamorous women in the world, Stewart expertly exposes the human cost of fame.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: It's hard not to be sucked into this deliciously irreverent spin on British Royalty that won't win any fans within the House of Windsor, but should win over any remaining Kristen Stewart skeptics.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: With radiant costuming and lush set design, Spencer is one of the most textured films of the year thus far.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: A film that spends nearly two hours advancing already axiomatic notions-obscene opulence does not equal freedom; protocol is a prison-with easy ironies, weighty symbols, and portentous phrases.
reviews.author: Melissa Anderson

reviews.text: A haunting, enthralling experience. Pablo Larraín delivers an exquisite film that's intimate & heartbreaking. But this is Kristen Stewart's film - a career-best performance. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Illustrates claustrophobia and panic and choking despair to slashing poetic effect... Pablo Larrain's Spencer makes no apologies for its mad movie-movie-ness.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: There is an adult's bitterness and knowingness that gives her Diana more gravitas than Stewart's previous characters. What's more, especially in some of Diana's more iconic outfits (she had many), she really does look like her.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Stewart is excellent. Her speech and mannerisms are uncanny at times.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: Taking an inventive, ambitious approach to a familiar story, writer Steven Knight and director Pablo Larrain elicit resonant emotions over just a few days in the life of Princess Diana.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Spencer is not the Diana biopic one would expect... But it's also one of the most ambitious, atmospheric, spellbinding cinematic works you'll see this year.
reviews.author: Stefania Sarrubba

reviews.text: You mostly can't look away from Stewart, or help yourself rooting for Di to live happily ever after. Personally, I hope Oscar takes the bait.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart brings all her formidable powers to bear, blazing through the screen with a flamboyant, heartsick chaos that sears through quiet dialogue and tense, terrible scenes of solitude.
reviews.author: Alison Lanier

reviews.text: With little narrative arc, the story is too thread-bare to keep us interested in this plausible depiction. In turn, Stewart's ability to then tap into Princess Diana's humanity and find a more layered persona to portray is thwarted.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Spencer itself is only a half-bad movie, promoting idolatry for a public that has lost respect for tradition and that has no sense of duty or sense of occasion.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: A trippy, disorienting, pulse-quickening experience
reviews.author: Jaime Davis

reviews.text: The problem with the movie is Larraín seems more concerned with standing out as an auteur director than telling a good story.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Larrain's film is a challenging and traumatic time at the movies. Stewart's Diana is living in a nightmare.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: It's quite captivating to watch as Pablo Larraín frees Stewart from nailing every pitch perfect quality about her. The focus is on reminding the audience of the deeply broken figure she became.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart and Pablo Larrain put us through the paces of a horror film about a woman trying to escape from a cult. We may call it royalty but Stewart's exquisite, claustrophobic performance has us longing for catharsis and oxygen.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: With Stewart's endearing lead role and Larraín's ability to create an environment that feels both beautiful and foreboding, Spencer is without a doubt one of the best films of 2021.
reviews.author: Cassie Hager

reviews.text: An oppressively gloomy mood piece... but the performance by Kristen Stewart is a career-topping breakthrough that will inevitably receive Oscar consideration.
reviews.author: Michael Medved

reviews.text: Larraín has created a fractured fairy tale, with a broken creature trapped in its center.
reviews.author: Ani Bundel

reviews.text: Handled like a Terrence Malick dream sequence in one moment, and a Kubrickian nightmare in another.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Larraín's vision anchored by Stewarts beauty and manic performance entertain and fascinate.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: Spencer is ultimately too similar: Two hours of celebrity voyeurism, watching a famous person's imagined private distress at a notorious personal low point.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Spencer is self-absorbed and monotonous, like a parody of a great art film rather than the real deal
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: A miscast Stewart merely plays dress-up, but it's Knight's heavy-handed script that truly dooms Larraín's film.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Pablo Larrain's psychological horror fantasy may catapult Kristen Stewart onto the Oscar dais.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: The tone recalls his previous film "Jackie," which I considered a masterpiece at the time, but how many tales do we need of famous women plunging into insanity, especially told through the same male gaze?
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Stewart's presence and emotional authenticity lends gravitas to this otherwise fairly slight look at the Princess of Wales.
reviews.author: Michael Dequina

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart gives one of the best performances of the year and of her career.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Spencer overcomes the occasional misstep in tone to deliver a moving film about a woman named Diana Spencer as opposed to the "People's Princess".
reviews.author: Cathy Brennan

reviews.text: Spencer is every bit as boring as the world of oppressive regimentation and stifling rituals it portrays.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: A penetrating psychological drama.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: This is one of the year's best pictures bar none.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Impressionistic, imaginative and immersive - I loved it.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: Stewart has completely disappeared into the role. She nails the voice and mannerisms but her ambitions extend far beyond mimicry.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Sensationalistic and rather tawdry...an alternately depressing and outlandish exercise in hysterical psycho-melodramatics.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Both compelling and irritating, sometimes simultaneously.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: The film's best performance belongs to the ever-realiable Timothy Spall, as a tough ex-military man hired to keep tabs on the ditzy Diana in what some definitely will be calling a hatchet job on a woman who became a legend long before her tragic death.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: A portrait of a person at the breaking point.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: What works comprises Kristen Stewart's striking performance as the beleaguered Princess. Her mannerisms, voice, visible pain intermix; it's difficult to look away from her even when particular scenes beg the viewer to do so.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: It works better when stared at and the message remains that we can't keep something graceful locked away. Like a beautiful butterfly, a powerful lion, or a wild horse. Spencer is something that should not be tamed.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Intimately capturing the agony of a woman trapped in an opulent prison, it's a film you won't soon shake.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Pablo Larraín and writer Steven Knight have crafted a tale of psychological horror as the audience watches a woman fight for the agency she needs to take back her life.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: . Larrain directs Kristen Stewart to her best film performance yet, in a film that is magnificently crafted, but so depressing to watch.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: We're in a time period where Diana has only about six more years on this Earth, but at least she was able to break free and hopefully experience a measure of happiness in the years after the imagined events of Spencer..
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: It's beautifully shot, really well-acted by Kristen Stewart, and has a fantastic score by Jonny Greenwood that I've already decided is my favorite of the year.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: Spencer allows viewers to become the support system Diana so sorely lacked at the time...
reviews.author: Becca James

reviews.text: Brilliant central performance. Sally Hawkins does a great job of taking this role, and turning it into a symbol of heartfelt love.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Larrain uses his considerable skills to create a change-resistant world in which, as someone puts it, there can be no past or future, only a ceremonial sameness. I guess that makes Spencer a sophisticated movie with a simple point...
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: At times, the film is excruciating, albeit deliberately, and that works it its favor.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: Technically, cinematographer Claire Mathon subtly creates and shifts moods with the tenor of scenes, and Johnny Greenwood's music changes to convey Diana's separation from the chilly royal family.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Stewart has played these women who are permanently on edge before, and it's rather wondrous how she manages to make them different from one another.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: While she neither looks nor sounds like Diana, Stewart nails the sense of her: meek, affected and sharper than she gets any credit for. The result is a fully-realized portrait of an overexposed woman that never falls into imitation or parody.
reviews.author: Cate Young

reviews.text: The film is gorgeous and meticulously nuanced, but this does not mean that it is emotionally urgent.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: I once wrote that Stewart had a narrow range and I have never been happier to eat my words.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: The film isn't concerned with how Diana died, but in how she decided to live.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: It's all too much, and then some. The script, by Steven Knight, is sprinkled with howlers that sound like they were recycled from Dynasty.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Best of all is Sally Hawkins as Diana's loyal dresser; their scene, laughing together on a beach, has the feel of a liberation from captivity, for both of them.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: Spencer is not as tight as director Larraín's previous biographical take Jackie, but Stewart gives an excellent performance as a woman, wife, mother, and human being smothered by the privilege she was born into and forced into.
reviews.author: Princess Weekes

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart is as good as advertised in Spencer, a well-produced wallow in the angst and sadness of Princess Diana.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: ...rueful moments of joy that don't seem cheapened by fictionalization, they instead seem like flourishes that bring Stewart's depiction of Diana the person to life.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: [Stewart] uses her innate awkwardness and reserved nature to turn in by far the best work of her career.
reviews.author: Owen Gabbey

reviews.text: Larraín, working from an imaginative screenplay by Steven Knight, fills his own frame with a story that is not quite biographical truth, neither wholly invented. But that is part of its genius.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: We're not watching The Crown. We're watching a full-on thriller.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: It's a potent fantasy just as intoxicating as the childhood stories we were told: a heroine that manages to defeat the monsters and gets to reign over her own life, if only for a moment.
reviews.author: Erin Strecker

reviews.text: This is a heist picture where it's her smile she's absconding -- she's stuffing her heart in her oversized pockets and smuggling it with the laundry
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: In Pablo Larraín's dreamlike movie, Diana is not the people's princess but a woman in search of herself.
reviews.author: Jo Livingstone

reviews.text: I never felt that the filmmakers were posthumously trying to cash in on Diana's celebrity. The fable-making, at least, is done with genuine commitment. Most of all, Stewart's fierce performance roots it all in reality.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: This is less an impersonation than it is a possession, and even though [Kristen Stewart] may not look precisely like Diana, she embodies her in a manner that is thoroughly convincing from start to finish.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: 'Spencer' feels like watching a both a tragedy suspended in time and a ghost story. Stewart's performance only enhances the heaviness that the audience will feel knowing how Diana's story plays out.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart mesmerizes in haunting portrait of Princess Diana.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Writer Steven Knight turns Di's life into a silly, dumb fairy tale made stylish by director Pablo Larraín. Stewart's moving performance redeems the caricature, as do Sally Hawkins as Di's beloved dresser and Timothy Spall as her malevolent royal handler.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: 'Spencer' employs an impeccable visual design and brilliant music with compartmentalized editing, and dashes of art and history, to paint an unconventional, yet universal picture.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Diana is a tragic figure, because previous generations tried to turn her into their idea of what a princess should be. Spencer turns her into what *our* enlightened generation wants her to be, which is right and proper.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: As a fictionalized narrative, it itches at spots that a documentary couldn't reach, and it conveys certain emotional truths that more straightforward attempts might gloss over.
reviews.author: Rich Juzwiak

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart is the best thing about the otherwise shallow Spencer.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Spencer isn't quite gaudy or excessive enough...and in this way, pales in comparison to Larraín's last couple projects which addressed similar ideas more creatively.
reviews.author: M.G. Mailloux

reviews.text: The casting, with Kristen Stewart as Princess Diana, is brilliant, and the ending, in a top-down convertible, is sublime. So why is the rest of Pablo Larraín's Spencer such a hollow exercise in high camp?
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: "Spencer" is a devastating and grotesque depiction of the iconic royal.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The film is a celebration of a woman who refused to colour within the lines and let her rainbow shine forth, consequences be damned.
reviews.author: Yasmin Omar

reviews.text: Director Pablo Larrain researched Diana for two years with dozens of interviews, has created a ghostly masterpiece.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Spencer feels in every way like a companion piece to Larraín's Jackie, both mesmeric suites about women trapped in a gilded cage of politics, privilege, and intense media scrutiny.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: Unlike JACKIE, Pablo Lorrain is content with a vague abyss for Diana, & not a fan of a Queenie Ghost. but Stewart is stellar & it ends grandly, & Pablo is always hella unique.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart is simply spectacular in the best performance of her career.
reviews.author: Max Covill

reviews.text: A career-best performance by Stewart and excellent tech credits across the board.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart is so good as Princes Diana-it's the performance of her life-that the Academy should start engraving her name on the Best Actress Oscar.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart stars in yet another major film from director Pablo Larrain, a modern master in cinema. Do not miss seeing the film on the big screen.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: Stewart's remarkable performance makes this "fable of true tragedy" - as it is prefaced - a wonder to watch.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: Mood and ambience are no substitute for a compelling story, and "Spencer" doesn't tell us one.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Who better to play a person remembered for her perceived shyness than the current maestro of hooded introspection?
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Whether she's "Diana" or not, Stewart's is one of the most mesmerizing performances of the year.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: My next sentence is something I never thought I would write but...Thank goodness for Kristen Stewart.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Unbalanced and unjust, "Spencer" is nonetheless perversely gripping. It dares to unbend, playing the angry fool amid kings-to-be, queens, princes, princesses, and all that jazz.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: It peels back the layers of Diana's struggles through immaculate filmmaking and a devastatingly beautiful performance from Kristen Stewart.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart gives a career-best performance, melting away into the role with the help of an immaculate team of make-up, hair and costume artists surrounding her
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Spencer is a haunting portrait of a woman on the brink of collapse, who is desperate to escape the stifling pressure of the Royal Family.
reviews.author: Nicole Ackman

reviews.text: What remains elusive is Diana's charisma, her natural star wattage that came out effortlessly in public.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: In Spencer, we see Spencer, the traumatized woman underneath the spotless gowns, in all her vulnerability, both the lows and the highs.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: Stewart, on the other hand, sells her character's state of mind. Her performance pierces the script's inclination towards melodrama.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: [Spencer] calls itself a "fable from a true tragedy." It might also be called a fever dream, a surreal nightmare, a reductio ad tedium or just an inherently limiting concept that slowly but inexorably squeezes the life out of itself.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Pablo Larraín's portrait of Diana uses her maddening experience as a reluctant member of the Royal Family to illustrate the stultifying and flattening experience of trying to remain sanguine in the face of a phlegmatic national culture.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: An opportunity wasted
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: In the title role, Kristen Stewart portrays Diana at a low point in the troubled princess' life, but Stewart's performance is the high point of this frequently repetitive and sometimes far-fetched film.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: It's also a good film-a very good one, in fact-that frequently threatens to be great, but it seldom lives up to the weighty themes promised by its dialogue, and it comes achingly close to scaling the heights Kristen Stewart reaches with her performance.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Director Pablo Larraín gives us beautiful images and a career-making performance by Kristen Stewart, with nothing at the core. Even though 'Spencer' has all the makings of a great film, it is quite boring.
reviews.author: Catalina Combs

reviews.text: Stewart has become a fine actor in recent years, and gives us a quite superb portrayal of a lost young woman, fragile but dogged, and determined to assert her humanity whatever the cost.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Spencer could have been a sordid hit piece, but Larraín gives us a taut, psychological drama that once again establishes him as peerless in the biopic game.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: Stewart both carries the film and the day. She looks nothing like Diana but is somehow Diana. I think it's called "great acting."
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: For all of Larraín's artistry, Spencer would crumble in the hands of the wrong actress, and Stewart gives one of the best performances of her career so far as this highly subjective version of Diana.
reviews.author: Mary Sollosi

reviews.text: Spencer is an extraordinary film, daring in its conception, strange and captivating in its execution, and with a performance by Kristen Stewart that feels, quite literally, out of this world.
reviews.author: Demetrios Matheou

reviews.text: Like the jazz that permeates Greenwood's music, Spencer is a riff on Diana with Larraín and Stewart operating at the peak of their powers.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: It's a historical fantasia, a claustrophobic thriller and a dark comedy of manners, all poised on a knife's edge between tabloid trash and high art.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: There is nothing about what Knight wrote or what Stewart plays that is specifically about Diana. The details are vague. This could be about any anonymous rich white lady trapped in a cult.
reviews.author: Murtada Elfadl

reviews.text: It leaves nearly every prominent biopic in the dust.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: A two-hour tightening of a piano wire. It's motorized by feeling and observation, like a Richard Linklater character study filtered through a Terrence Malick lens. It's an experience, plain and simple, and a difficult one to shake.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: It's weird, but it works. Just be prepared for one wild, sometimes out-of-control, ride with Stewart always showing a steady hand on the steering wheel.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Dealing in the claustrophobia of royalty, Larraín crafts Spencer as a suffocating chamber-piece; a haunted house movie where our hero is tormented by the spirit of tradition.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: "Spencer" is more than the portrait of a woman in distress. If it's a fable, it's a political fable, an allegory of powerlessness, revolt and liberation.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: While Kristen Stewart's career might have begun with roles as a child actress and her tenure in Twilight, her tour-de-force performance in Spencer shows how she's grown into a Hollywood leading lady.
reviews.author: Corey Chichizola

reviews.text: The kind of movie where you should just sit down and just go along for the ride on which [Pablo] Larrain wants to take you.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: All of this is a decidedly one-note affair, but to be fair, Larraín plays that note with such confidence that there's at least some stylistic nuance to it.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart gives the performance of her career. Her work as Diana is both layered and compassionate.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Stewart and Larraín compellingly capture the essence of Diana's life through a lens of terror and existential dread, cementing 'Spencer' as one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: Larraín thinks in bold, often abstract images and concepts that don't always sit well alongside conventionally scripted scenes.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: You watch wishing this story, in the real world, could have had a different ending; and marveling at how Stewart finds new, close-to-the-bone layers in a character we thought we already knew.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: There's more than one way to dramatize the public/private schisms of celebrity, and this way feels right for this director, this actress and this movie.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: "A fable from a true tragedy," the opening text promises, promisingly. Yet Spencer is airless as drama, every bit as hemmed in by its schematic design as Diana is by her life in the blinding spotlight.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: There's a poignant ending waiting for viewers, but the journey there isn't quite as profound as it initially appears to be.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The film I couldn't get out of my head while trying to process Spencer - stirring up the deepest currents in the subconscious, unblinking, raw and red - is Marina de Van's In My Skin.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: [Stewart's] interpretation of Diana is risky, but it is also the glue that holds this brilliantly odd and lavishly shot film together.
reviews.author: Josh Kupecki

reviews.text: Despite a rather joyous finale, Spencer has more to do with a psychological horror film than a traditional biopic.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Rarely does a writer of movies put a stamp on a film like Knight does here, slipping grandly loaded lines into the mouths of not always famously articulate characters.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: This an enjoyably strange spectacle, perhaps best appreciated by taking it less seriously than its creators intended.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: The symbolism throughout is so heavy-handed as almost to impress in the end, for sheer bone-headedness.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: Stewart is perfect as the angsty, tortured Diana, carefully captured by Claire Mathon's camera, bathed in cold English light.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: The movie is bleak yet funny, depressing yet uplifting, and it's to Stewart's credit that she rides these emotions seamlessly.
reviews.author: Danny Brogan

reviews.text: There is interaction with people who are caricatures of people, and joyless robots who are supposed to represent the Royals. Spencer makes a convincing case that an invitation to Christmas with the Queen might not be any fun at all.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: "Spencer" knows that Diana is headed on a tragic path. Its triumph is that it allows her one last joyride- rooftop down, arms in the air- to break free before the inevitable comes knocking.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The divergence from reality here allows Larraín to twist Diana into the character he wants to depict, and push Spencer in the direction of a moody, ghostly fairytale.
reviews.author: Aurora Amidon

reviews.text: Once you get past how Stewart captures Diana's look and spirit, there's not much more to see or learn.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart delivers a career-best...performance in Spencer, a film closer to psychological nightmare than biopic.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: The point of Spencer seems to be not to reveal Diana the real person, but to treat her differently in a cinematic sense - to recast her in a different kind of movie than the ones that we've already seen.
reviews.author: Linda Holmes

reviews.text: Through it all, Stewart is fearless as Diana.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: ...Stewart nails Diana's mannerisms, but making fantastical films about public figures isn't easy, and Spencer doesn't have the narrative smoke and mirrors required to charm or persuade....
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Knight and Larrain have fallen into the trap of disclosing all the salaciousness we've learned over the years about Diana, but with no allotted time for understanding and sympathy.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: While Spencer is not a great film, it does give Stewart the opportunity to carry the story of a major historical figure-- and she does it (pun intended) royally.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: 'Spencer' is a gothic melodrama with an awards-worthy performance from Kristen Stewart.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: The acting is outstanding all the way around. But Stewart is brilliant.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: For better and for worse, "Spencer" conveys one thing quite powerfully: the feeling of living in a rarefied, indifferent world that doesn't seem to value independent women, much less people.
reviews.author: Hau Chu

reviews.text: Mesmerizing! A spellbinding psychological journey into the heart, mind and soul of a troubled human being who yearns to break free. Kristen Stewart gives a raw, transcendent performance. She deserves an Oscar.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Spencer is a gorgeous, evocative, and hauntingly poetic glimpse into a woman's mind at its most panic-stricken, its most fearful, its most empowered.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: The perceived blame of this antagonism falling squarely on Diana's shoulders can't help but be reminiscent of the column inches spent criticizing Stewart for not smiling, and the utter ownership hardcore fans felt they had at the height of Twilight.
reviews.author: Rosie Fletcher

reviews.text: It's as painful and sorrowful a biopic as they come, but not without resiliency as Diana slowly stands up for herself; Kristen Stewart is mesmerizing and delivers one of the year's best performances
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: With a stellar performance from Kristen Stewart, director Pablo Larraín's supremely brilliant "Spencer" is an enlightening glimpse into the mind of Princess Diana that doubles as an effective horror film.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Though it doesn't ever make you really feel, Spencer is a bold, compassionate, poetic riposte to standard royal biopics. It  also confirms Kristen Stewart as one of the most exciting actors working today.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: It is a sign of a strong performance when we forget that we are watching the actor giving it, something Kristen Stewart accomplishes within the opening minutes of this fictional psychological portrait of the iconic Princess of Wales.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: It takes one of the most promising screen actresses of her generation and casts her out to sea with nothing to hold onto but a hideous script that's all attitude without depth or understanding.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: If you still think Kristen Stewart's a bad actress (Twilight!) see Spencer to understand why she continues to be a world-dominating movie star. One does not simply walk into Mordor or Hollywood and stick around for as long as she has for no good reason.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: This nightmarish look at a Christmas with the Royals is a heartbreaker, thanks to some very savvy storytelling, as well as Kristin Stewart's stunner of a performance.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Spencer is an analysis on whether "faking it till you make it" can work for every spirit. #diandrareviews
reviews.author: Diandra Reviews

reviews.text: Uneven if beautiful.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: This is admittedly total fiction with real people doing nothing they ever did. Despite fine performances by Spall and Stewart, it's akin to Shakespeare's hit job on Richard III
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: In Pablo Larrain's vision of Diana Spencer, she is not a Barbie, so much as an old school print cut-out doll, with endless new outfits to put on and take off.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: Sigh. What a waste of talent; everyone deserves better.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: It's not realism as much as Gothic horror with a dying Princess at the center. The film is about the loss of identity and Stewart's rendering of a woman stuck in an unending nightmare she can see no way out of. It's heartbreaking.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: As a day in the tragic, overwhelming life of Princess Diana, Spencer is spectacular.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: It's a laser-focused study of a woman at her breaking point and Stewart does her best screen work to date in bringing the terribly fragile, young woman to pained life.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Spencer is the most beautifully shot film of the year, with a career-best performance from Kristen Stewart, who embodies Diana's mannerisms, accent, and demeanor with incredible emotional depth.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: Heavy-handed and unnecessarily long, Spencer explores Diana as a prisoner of the royal family in heart-wrenching and beautifully haunting fashion.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: Larrain's direction is impeccable, with the gorgeous cinematography and lavish production design turning Sandringham into a more opulent Overlook Hotel.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: Spencerwill be looked at as that odd Princess Diana movie that Kristen Stewart was really great in that one time.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Stewart, while not quite offering an eerie copy of the princess's mannerisms, offers a magnificent portrayal of a woman who's forced by those around her to be an obedient introvert when she wants nothing more than be a happy-go-lucky extrovert.
reviews.author: Boyd van Hoeij

reviews.text: Spencer has little to say outside these ideas, but it says them with such gusto that it gives Kristen Stewart a new way to shine.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: [Kristen Stewart] embodies Diana with a composed ferocity that is uniquely Stewart's but feels right for a woman in Diana's situation.
reviews.author: Aly Caviness

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart completely disappears. Spencer should bag her an Oscar, Golden Globe and everything else in between
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart is vulnerable and resilient in this portrait of Princess Diana and her ostracism from the royal family.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Strained and brittle to the point of shattering, through gesture, body language, tense glances and superbly clipped delivery Stewart carries the film on slender shoulders, fierce yet fragile.
reviews.author: Matthew Anderson

reviews.text: The filmmakers are obviously reverential towards Princess Diana, but they frequently fall into the same sensationalized traps that marred a lot of the media coverage during the subject's lifetime.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: It's part costume drama, part psychological thriller and part gothic horror. Seriously.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: I sobbed the whole way home.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Spencer is a powerful, gorgeously shot and well-acted psychological drama from Pablo Larraín with a top-form turn from Kristen Stewart - but may prove too uncomfortable for some.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: A fraught drama that suffers from its slow pacing and uncompromising tone but [Kristen] Stewart delivers a staggering performance that demands attention during the awards season.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: There's an overarching sense of authenticity, some satirical bite, and never has a royal retreat seemed more like a prison.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Coupled with Stewart's exposed nerve of a performance, the suffocating intensity of Larraín's filmmaking, and Jonny Greenwood's droning score, the movie brings a fresh sense of tragedy and loss to a tale that might otherwise feel familiar.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Rather than trying to hide behind complete imitation, Stewart harnesses a careful symbiosis that incorporates who she is with who Diana was and must have been, and in that fusion lies an enrapturing cohabitation of spirits that one cannot look away from.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: The proposal's riskiness exceeds such perilous expectations. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Tébar

reviews.text: It's all pure fantasy porn, absolutely defiant of reality with no subtlety whatsoever.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart embodies the distraught Lady Diana in Pablo Larraín's Spencer, an audacious chamber piece that fetishizes the woman it seeks to liberate.
reviews.author: Ana Yorke

reviews.text: Stewart's uncanny magnetism-her ability to mesmerize the camera even in moments of stillness or repose-keeps it watchable even in moments of extreme silliness.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Larraín admits up front it's more fable than fact and, while he occasionally overreaches with his myth-spinning, his empathy and compassion for a woman suffering a mental breakdown are beautifully expressed.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Spencer is a film that completely hinges on its lead performance, and I'm happy to say that Kristen Stewart not only rose to the task, but exceeded every expectation.
reviews.author: Amanda the Jedi

reviews.text: With Stewart's breathtaking performance, this is a film that truly demonstrates how cinema can elevate any story, no matter how familiar, in ways that no other artistic medium can.
reviews.author: Wilson Kwong

reviews.text: The film is Stewart's to carry, and she does it by going less minimalist than is her habit and by allowing an awareness of the absurdity of Diana's situation to seep in, even as she plays the woman's suffering entirely straight.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Princess Diana wanders through the ornate but empty halls of theSandringham Estate, a living ghost in an expensive gown.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Spencer is Kristen Stewart's finest hour and an hypnotically immersive experience. Stewart deserves to win the Oscar for Best Actress, full stop.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: [It] gets to the meat of what was tormenting the People's Princess better than any simple historical retelling ever could.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Spencer is an act of psychological horror, a kind of ghost story, and a survivalist picture carried by an uncannily immersive Kristen Stewart, in the best performance of her career.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Like its enigmatic and tragic subject, the late Diana, Princess of Wales, Spencer will haunt you.
reviews.author: Glenn Sumi

reviews.text: The best performances are those that find a perfect fusion between character and star persona
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: Stewart disappears into the role, but it's in the moments where she's allowed to be herself that Spencer rings true.
reviews.author: Chandler Levack

reviews.text: Pablo Larraín's film readily conjures a paranoia-suffused atmosphere of fear for what might happen at any moment.
reviews.author: Mark Hanson

reviews.text: The film is composed of private conversations, anecdotes, fantasies, flashbacks that most likely did not take place but add up to a hypnotic collage of impressions that brings you closer to a very special person.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: Kristin Stewart's immersive performance as the tragic princess - with a strong assist from Jacqueline Duran's costumes - transforms the film into a sort of fairy tale/ghost story imagining what could have happened.
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: Spencer is, like The Last of England, not subtle, though it does manage in the end a kind of sublimity.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart is a fantastic choice for this Diana, superb at conveying emotion through small expressions. She radiates charisma befitting the woman herself, with a little help from the luminous lens of Claire Mathon.
reviews.author: Tom Bond

reviews.text: Showing how the dream of being a rich and beautiful princess curdled into a nightmare might sound like a hard sell, but Spencer pulls it off in heightened, claustrophobic and truly decadent fashion.
reviews.author: Sophie Monks Kaufman

reviews.text: Pablo Larraín's sublime new film about [Princess Diana], in which she is played by a career-best Kristen Stewart, is a fitting and fantastic tribute.
reviews.author: Adam Solomons

reviews.text: What Larraín and Knight bring to Diana's story is a daringness to imagine the woman not only outside of her public context, but her media-constructed one.
reviews.author: Cassie da Costa

reviews.text: An empathetic, intelligent insight into the prison of fame and privilege, with Kristen Stewart offering a lead performance that is brittle, tender, sometimes playful and not a little uncanny.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: Stewart does terrific work as this royal-turned-scream-queen, but one does get the sense that she could be even better were "Spencer" to allow the character to go as wild as everything else does around her.
reviews.author: Ben Croll

reviews.text: Kristen Stewart's exemplary performance elevates this intriguing and visually stunning portrait of a young woman standing in a hurricane, looking for a rock to cling to.
reviews.author: Jo-Ann Titmarsh

reviews.text: Like the austere artwork in the Sandringham House, the film deserves to be framed and hung on a wall. Admire it, don't embrace it. Maybe that's the point.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: A haunting reimagining of a tense Christmas holiday in the life of Princess Diana.
reviews.author: Monica Castillo

reviews.text: This is a film that will potentially delight, challenge, and force its wide target audience to take seriously on its own terms. A dream ballet of a dying star.
reviews.author: David Katz

reviews.text: You can see a lot of Kristen Stewart in Diana and vice versa. Stewart gives us an inside look into the mind of Diana and what it is like to live a life that is constantly being monitored and controlled by others.
reviews.author: Scott Menzel

reviews.text: Spencer left me with only one overwhelming sentiment: bring on the new series of The Crown.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Larraín turns this Diana into exactly the thing the royal family accused the real-life Diana of being, a willful and pouty constant complainer.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: An odd but successful immersion into the emotional distress of woman lost to herself and trapped in a chilly, regimented glass house.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Stewart is such inspired casting that she makes all this eccentric nonsense watchable.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: Stewart's febrile, sensitive performance and Larraín's trademark lyricism give it an emotional kick that such predecessors lacked.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Its focus rests on its heroine alone. But what a heroine - and what thrillingly gutsy, seductive, uninhibited filmmaking this is.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: All the right people are going to hate "Spencer." That's just how good it is.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: It is often witless and banal, leaving Larraín and the actors to heroically milk the drama from a string of interactions that are either overstuffed with "meaning", or just deathly dull.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: Stewart adopts the blonde bob, the Kensington clothes and the breathy voice but stops short of full impersonation and her performance is better for it.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: Stewart is impressive, melting away at times to play this "magnet of madness", as Diana calls herself.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: At once a work of great sensitivity and high, hilarious camp, less interested in identifying the 'real' Diana than in building a living, breathing character.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: I can't say enough about Stewart's performance, steering from impression of an impossibly well-chronicled figure to beautifully achieving the essence of who she was.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: The Princess Diana story is given an art house makeover in this infuriating mixed bag, one that veers wildly from moments of dreamy intrigue to risible scenes of camp.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Stewart's finely detailed work on the accent and mannerisms is impeccable. The camera adores her, and she has seldom been more magnetic, or more heartbreakingly fragile.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Unfurls in a torrent of ideas and madness, some of it brilliant, some of it quite silly.
reviews.author: Jason Solomons

reviews.text: Larraín's approach to the material is rich and intoxicating and altogether magnificent.
reviews.author: Xan Brooks

reviews.text: An enthralling drama of Diana's moment of truth and transition.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

synopsis: The marriage of Princess Diana and Prince Charles has long since grown cold. Though rumors of affairs and a divorce abound, peace is ordained for the Christmas festivities at the Queen's Sandringham Estate. There's eating and drinking, shooting and hunting. Diana knows the game. But this year, things will be profoundly different. SPENCER is an imagining of what might have happened during those few fateful days.
